full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be; stated thus, the present opposite party No.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted the Title Suit No.124 of 2006 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Chatkhil, Noakhali against the present petitioners and opposite parties No.3-40 impleading them as defendants praying for declaration of title and further declaration that the deed of exchange Nos. 22 and 23 dated 2-1-1971 are forged, fraudulent, collusive and not acted upon contending infer alia, that the suit land appertaining to CS khatian No.359 corresponding to SA khatian No.372 measuring an area of 77 decimals of land in plot No.1735 under Mouza Topga originally belonged to one Yousuf Mollah who died leaving behind three daughters namely Syedunnessa, Rubitunnessa and Faridunnessa. Yousuf Mollah had another daughter namely Khairunnessa who died before him. The SA khatian was prepared in the name of Yousuf Mollah. He executed a waqf deed being No.782 dated 4-3-1916 in the name of his aforesaid three daughters and one grandson namely Ahmed Ullah. Saydunncssa died leaving behind three sons Waziullah, Aman Ullah, Fazley Rahman and one daughter Fatema Begum. By amicable settlement, Syedunnessa got 77 decimals of land of suit plot No.1735 and at the demise of Syedunnessa her property was amicably settled among her heirs and the suit plot No.1735 fallen into the saham of Waziulla, who died leaving behind two sons namely Mustafizur Rahman and Enaytur Rahman and they were owning and possessing the same. The son of Syedunnessa namely Fazlur Rahman died leaving, three sons namely Abdul Momen, Abdul Matin and Harunur Rashid. Abdul Matin died leaving behind two sons Mizanur Rahman and Muksudur Rahrrlan and two daughters namely Noorjahan Begum and Shahinur Begum. The son of Syedunnessa namely Amanullah died leaving behind three sons namely Mostafa, Helal Uddin, Zahiruddin and two daughters Shefali Begum and Shetera Begum. Rabitunnessa died leaving one son Aman Ullah and one daughter Halima Begum. That the son Faridunnessa Abdul Fattah died leaving behind one son Tariqul Islam and two daughters Kamrun Nahar, Ohidun Nahar. The son of Faridunnessa namely Abdur Rahim died leaving one son Abul Khair and one daughter Ajkarnessa and in this way the plaintiffs are the heirs of Waziullah, the son of Syedunnessa. The other heirs of Syedunnessa i.e, the defendant's No. 34-51 and Waziullah got 77 decimals of land in suit plot No.1735. In the suit land the defendants had no right, title and possession but they are claiming the suit land by way of collusive exchange deeds. Further case of the plaintiffs is such that after getting the certified copy of the deeds, they came to know that one Mobarakullah and Nurul Amin being the1st party exchanged the suit land with one ABM Takdir Hossain Bhuiyan showing him, in party but in fact the 1st party had no right, title and possession in the land of exchange it appears from the certified copy of the deed that Takdir Hossain Chowdhury, son of Alhaj Ramjan Ali Miazi is the recipient of the said deed and not Takdir Hossain Bhuiyan, son of Ator Ali. On the basis of the aforesaid collusive deed of exchange the defendants denied the title of the plaintiffs which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendants No.2, 4, 6, 18-21, 25, 26, 28 and 32 in short is thus, that the suit land is situated at Mouza-Topga under Police Station-Ramganj of District Noakhali which is recorded in CS khatian No.359, MRR No.372,plot No.1735 and total area 77 decimals out of38.50 acres of land. Further case of the contesting defendants is such that 1 anna, 6 gandas, 2 koras, 2 krantis were recorded in the name of Abdur Rashid and 2 annas, 13 gandas, 1kara, 1 kranti was recorded in the name of Abdul Latif and the rest 12 annas was recorded in the name of Yusuf Mollah. That non suited land of the said khatian of plot No.1179 measuring an area of 26 decimals was recorded in the name of Abdur Rashid and plot No.1180 comprising an area of 24 decimals was recorded in. the name of Yusuf Mollah and in plot No.1201 comprising an area of 76 decimals, In plot No.1306 an area of 19 decimals, in plot No.1316 an area of 42 decimals arid in plot No.1318 an area of 62 decimals was recorded in the name of Yusuf Mollah and the suit plot No.1735 comprising an area of 76 decimals of land was recorded in the name of Yusuf Mollah and thus Yusuf Mollah become the owner of 2.38 acres of land in all. Subsequently, Yusuf Mollah died leaving behind four daughters namely Jamila Khatun @ Khairunnessa, Syedunnessa, Rahimunnessa and Faridunnessa. Jamila Khatun @ Khairunnessa was married with one Raja Mia and she was living with her husband. Those other three daughters of Yusuf Mollah got married but they use to live in their father's residence. At the time of preparation of MR Rkhatian No.372 the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of two daughters and legal heirs of one daughter omitting the name of Jamila @ Khairunnessa. By amicable settlement Jamila Khatun @ Khairunnessa got 38.50 acres of the suit land and for such wrong record, the right of Jamila Khatun @ Khairunnessa was extinguished. Jamila Khatun died leaving behind two sons Mobarakullah and Siddiqullah. Siddiqullah died leaving behind one son Nurul Amin. Mobarakullah and Nurul Amin have been owning and possessing 38.50 acres of land of suit plot No.1735 for about 40 years. Thereafter, on 2-1-1971 they made two exchange deeds being No. 22 and 23 with one ABM Takdir Hossain Bhuiyan and they made over possession of the suit land to Takdir Hossain. Thereafter Takdir Hossain died leaving behind the defendants No. 25-12 who had been owning and possessing the suit land for about 32 years. The plaintiffs had no right, title, possession in the suit land in any manner. Besides this, there exist a road to the eastern side of the suit plot which include 41/2decimals of land and 34 decimals was owned and possessed by defendants No.25-32 and in the recent survey khatian No.747, Plot No. 6033 was recorded in the names of defendants No.25-32. The plaintiffs did not file any objection under sections 30/31 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1955. The plaintiffs had no right, title and possession in the suit land. The plaintiffs have no locus standi to file the suit. 

 8. The learned counsel on behalf of the petitioners during his argument submits that the plaintiffs in their testimony admits that the record of right stands recorded in the name of the defendants. The so called possession witnesses of the plaintiffs are not competent, credible, disinterested and trustworthy. The witness No.1 is the plaintiffs No.1 himself and the witnesses No.2-4 are the possession Witnesses of the plaintiffs who has totally failed to establish the plaintiff's possession, right and title over the suit land. On the contrary the defendants in support of their case have adduced 5(five) witnesses who have successfully proved the case of the defendants as stated within the contents of their pleadings. All the title documents of the defendants have been marked as Exhibits after proof without objection and there are no discussions and findings of the courts below on the said documents which has been proved and marked as Exhibits without objection. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the defendants in respect of the suit land mutated their names and have been paying rents regularly to the government. In respect of 'Ga' schedule land of the plaint the plaintiffs are claiming title but the land as described in that schedule is without specification and, as such, under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act the plaintiff's suit is barred. The deeds of exchange which has been challenged from the side of the plaintiffs in the suit were not challenged earlier and as a result of that under Article 91 of the Limitation Act as within three years from the date of the documents those were not challenged, the plaintiff's claim is barred by limitation. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the argument  advanced from the side of the learned Advocate for the petitioners and submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and Its subsequent appeal after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law decided all the matters-in-issue concurrently in favour of the plaintiffs and against the defendants. The learned Advocate further submits that there is no illegality or irregularity and no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. The learned Advocate also submits that the deeds of exchange which are the basic documents of the defendants are forged, created and not acted upon which would be apparent from the name of the executant of the deed and from the deposition of the witness No. 1 of the defendants and thus it is clear that the executant is a fictitious person. The certified copy of the deed being No. 3039 has been falsified from the defendant Md Zahangir Hossain who has stated that Yousuf Mollah left behind four daughters namely Khairunnessa @ Jamila, Syedunnessa, Rabidunnessa and Farid-un-nessa. He further states that Khairunnessa @ Jamila lived with her husband Raja Miah separately and the MRR Khatian was prepared omitting her name but the recent khatian has been prepared in the name of his brother Takdir Hossain Bhuiyan. From the face of the documents it appears that not Takdir Hossain Bhuiyan but one Takdir Hossain Chowdhury, son of Alhaj Ramjan Ali Miazi is the recipient of the deed No.3039 which has been marked as Exhibit-4 and the matter has been properly addressed by the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the courts below in their observation and findings concurrently decided that the deeds of exchange are forged, collusive and manipulated. The learned Court have cited some reasons within the findings which are consistent with the evidence on records and, as such, there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. 

 13. I have come across the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties that to substantiate the plaintiff's case they have adduced four witnesses. The witness No. 1 is the plaintiff No.1 himself Md Mostafizur Rahman. The plaintiff No. 1 in his testimony admits at a stage that the deeds of exchange are of more than 38/39 years and the recent survey was completed in their area in the year 1990-91 and the suit land of SA plot No.1735 has been recorded in recent survey as plot No.6033 and in 41/2 decimals of land of the suit plot there is a road by which the villagers move. He also admits that in the recent settlement plot No.6033, 34 decimals, of land have been included in field survey khatian No.2019 and in DP khatian No.787 which has been prepared in the name of the defendant's father and against that they did not file any case under sections 30/31 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In respect of the disputed exchange deeds the plaintiff No.1 states that his father died in the year 1993 and the deeds were executed and registered in the year 1971. During the life time of his father he did not file any case and after 40 years of the deeds they have 'instituted the original suit. Admittedly, the plaintiffs have failed to produce any Rent Receipt showing payment of rent in respect of the suit land and as regard their possession the witnesses who deposed as witness Nos. 2,3,4 and 5 tried to establish the case of the plaintiffs but from the examination-in-chief of these witnesses it is apparent from the face of the papers that the witnesses have failed to describe the actual identity of the suit land including its specification and as regard boundary they have totally failed to state anything. On the other hand, the defendants in support of their case have adduced five witnesses and among them DW1 is the defendant No.26 who tried to corroborate their pleading in his testimony. It is to be noticed that the established principle of civil law is such that it is the plaintiffs who in order to obtain a decree in their favour shall have to discharge their onus in proving their case, but on critical analysis of evidence I find that in respect of title and possession of the plaintiffs they have totally failed to prove their case by any tangible evidence and the evidence led from their side is not at all trustworthy, credible and competent. 

 16. In the instant case; as I have already referred to above, that in respect of a particular portion or land described in schedule 'ga' of the plaint the plaintiffs have sought for a declaration of title and the witnesses have totally failed to discharge their onus in proving the respective case of the plaintiffs as to their alleged possession and identification of the land. Besides this, having gone through the impugned judgment and decree it is evident to note that the lower appellate court i.e. the learned District Judge, Noakhali at the time of disposal of the appeal on merit have utterly failed to assess the evidence on records and there is no discussion of evidence and no sifting of the same in its true perspective. Under the ambit of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure it is the incumbent duty upon the appellate court below while affirming or reversing the judgment of the trial court that, the appellate court shall state the reasons for the decision after proper evaluation and assessment of evidence on records. Our Apex Court in the case of Hajarilal Mondal vs Md Mozaffor Bepari reported in 8 BLC (AD) 77 held that it is the principle of law that the lower appellate court being the final court of fact will have to discuss and re-assess the evidence on records independently while either reversing or affirming the findings of the trial court. But in the instant case as I have cited above that the learned District Judge have totally failed to scan the evidence on records by his discussion and evaluation of both oral and documentary evidence.
